reading.rtitle: It Is Essential That the Master Be Present
paras: Port state control exists because a flag state cannot inspect a ship that is never in its waters. The rules require that every ship in a member port be open to inspection. Any deficiency found is recorded against the ship, not against the inspector who found it. Detention follows only when the officer thinks the ship is not seaworthy.

The convention requires that the master notify the maritime authority at once about any problem with seaworthiness. It also recommends that all crew members complete the drill before departure. Look at the verbs: notify and complete, not notifies and completes. After requires, recommends and it is essential that, formal English uses the base form.

A surveyor may issue a certificate and an endorsement. But the surveyor may not decide that a deficiency is unimportant. That decision belongs to the authority, so a person who never saw the ship reviews each detention.

Critics say that a ship can have every certificate and still be unseaworthy on the day of the inspection. That is true. But port state control does something useful: the ship with the problem pays for it, in that port, on that day. It is essential that it stay that way.

paras: For a long time, a standard of measurement was an object. The metre was a metal bar kept near Paris, and the kilogram was a metal cylinder kept next to it. Anyone could, in theory, go and look at them.

The problem with an object is that it changes. Over a hundred years, the kilogram cylinder lost a little mass, or its copies gained some. Nobody could say which, because the cylinder was the definition. It is essential that a standard be independent of the thing it measures.

In 2019, scientists found a solution. They defined the units with constants of nature. The kilogram now depends on the Planck constant, and the metre on the speed of light. Nothing is kept in a safe, and any good laboratory can produce the units.
The new definitions are not more accurate for everyday use. A kitchen scale is as good as before. The real change is that the system no longer depends on one piece of metal.

listenings.text: People often ask me if I enjoy detaining ships. I have detained eleven ships in nine years, and I did not enjoy it once. My decision is very narrow. I record what I find. If the lifeboat gear was not serviced, that is a deficiency, and it goes on the record. The master can agree or not. But I do not decide if it matters. The rules require that every deficiency be recorded against the ship. Detention is a different decision. A person in an office, who never saw the ship, reviews it. That is not a weakness. It is the design of the system.
